summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, John S. Strong earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Frank E. Reynolds. He was Charles A. Dana Professor Emeritus of Religious Studies at Bates College.
John Sampson was a linguist and Indologist who received degrees from the University of Liverpool and the University of Oxford. He served as Librarian at the University of Liverpool from 1892 to 1928.

Indologist and linguist John Scudder Chandler studied at Yale University. He served as acting principal at Pasumalai Seminary (1890–1892), Fellow at the University of Madras (1913–1922), and director of the Language School at Kodaikanal (1924–1928).

John Shakespear was an Indologist and linguist who studied under John Richardson and at Wellington College and Sandhurst. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Sandhurst (1805–1809) and Professor of Hindustani at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
Active in Indology and history, John Shore succeeded William Jones and served as President of The Asiatic Society in 1794.

John Shortt was a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Madras Medical College and the University of Aberdeen. He served as Assistant Apothecary for the East India Company and Assistant Surgeon at the University of Madras (1854–1878).

John Sinclair Stevenson was a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Clifton College, Lincoln College, the University of Edinburgh, and Princeton Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary for the Presbyterian Church in Ireland from 1894 to 1924.
John Snelling was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as editor of The Middle Way from around 1979 to 1988 and General Secretary of the Buddhist Society from around 1980 to 1984.

Indologist and linguist John Stevenson studied at Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as a Scottish Missionary Society missionary, East India Company Chaplain (1834–1854), and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1853–1855).

Indologist and religious studies scholar John Stirling Morley Hooper studied at the University of Oxford and Corpus Christi College. He served as Headmaster at Wesley Higher Secondary School in 1930 and General Secretary of the Bible Society of India in 1941.

Linguist John Strachan studied at Aberdeen, Cambridge, and Jena, where he was taught by Berthold Delbrück and Rudolf Thurneysen. He was Professor of Greek (1885) and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology (1889) at Owens College.

John Stratton Hawley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Amherst College and completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served at Bowdoin College and became Claire Tow Professor of Religion at Columbia University around 1986.
John Stuart Mill worked in philosophy and history. He studied at University College London from 1829 to 1830 and served at the East India Company from approximately 1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall was a historian who studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and Leiden University. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1936 to 1941.

John Taber is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He taught at Case Western Reserve University (1983–1989) and joined the University of New Mexico around 1989.
John Taylor was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned his M.D. from the University of Edinburgh by 1804 and served with the London Missionary Society between 1805 and 1807.

Indologist John Thayer Hitchcock earned degrees from Amherst, Chicago, Connecticut, and Cornell. He held posts at Amherst, UC Berkeley, UCLA, and was Professor of Anthropology and South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1966 to 1982.

John Thompson Platts was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford, he held posts at Benares College, Saugor High School, and became Teacher of Persian at Oxford in 1880.

Indologist and linguist John Van Someren Pope studied at the University of Cambridge. He served as a professor at Presidency University from approximately 1876 to 1889 and as Reader in Modern East Indian Languages at Trinity College Dublin in 1913.
Indologist and linguist John Victor Boulton studied at SOAS University of London, earning a Ph.D. around 1963–1967. He also served at SOAS as Lecturer in Bengali and Oriya from 1962 to 1988.
